claim: Across meta-analyses, deliberate practice (as broadly coded) correlates with performance at roughly r=.35-.43 overall, i.e. about 12-18% of variance (post-corrigendum 2014 figure: r=.38, 14%), far below the 'largely accounted for' claim of 1993.
agent_test: Not applicable to inference-time agent; background.
audit_note: Macnamara 2014 (r=.35, 12%), Macnamara 2016 sports (r=.43, 18%) and Macnamara and Hambrick 2020 (post-corrigendum r=.38, 14%) all match; sports corrected to .45/20% in the 2020 table.

claim: The size of the effect depends strongly on domain: after the 2018 corrigendum deliberate practice explains about 24% of variance in games, 23% in music, 20% in sports, 5% in education and 1% in professions (original 2014 values: r=.51, .46, .42, .21, .05).
agent_test: None; domain-dependence is a reminder that gains from 'practice-like' loops will vary by task predictability.
audit_note: The r values (games .51, music .46, sports .42, education .21, professions .05) are the original 2014 figures that the 2018 corrigendum superseded; post-corrigendum variance shares are games 24%, music 23%, sports 20%, education 5%, professions 1%, inconsistent with K01 which uses post-corrigendum values.
claim_before_audit: The size of the effect depends strongly on domain: games and music highest (r about .46-.51), sports about .42, education about .21, professions near zero.

claim: Effect shrinks as task predictability falls (high r=.49, moderate .35, low .21), so practice explains more where the task is stable and rule-bound.
agent_test: Compare scaffold gain on stable-rule tasks vs open-ended tasks at equal tokens.

claim: The size of the effect depends on how deliberate practice is defined and corrected. Strict definitions (solitary or coached, no team practice or lectures) give r=.54 uncorrected (Ericsson and Harwell, 29% of variance; Platz music observed .54, corrected .61), and Ericsson and Harwell's attenuation correction raises this to 61% of variance (r about .78) only under assumed reliabilities (.6 practice, .8 performance) that Macnamara and Hambrick dispute; broad definitions give r about .35-.43. Part of the disagreement is definitional and part is the reliability correction.
audit_note: Platz music r=.54 is observed (corrected .61) and Ericsson and Harwell's r=.54 is uncorrected (29% of variance; their corrected figure is 61% of variance, r about .78 under assumed reliabilities), so 'r=.54-.61 (corrected)' mislabels the figures; Macnamara and Hambrick also show the correction depends on assumed reliability, so not all disagreement is definitional.
claim_before_audit: The size of the effect depends on how deliberate practice is defined. Strict definitions (solitary or coached, no team practice or lectures) give r=.54-.61 (corrected); broad definitions give r about .35-.43. Much of the disagreement is definitional.

claim: Correcting for unreliability of retrospective practice estimates raises r a lot, but the reliability value is assumed (0.6-0.9) and drives the result; the 'true' share of variance is between about 18% and 64-76% depending on that assumption.

Among elite performers the correlation between practice and rank falls to about r=.11 (1% of variance) in sports; critics of the theory read this as a ceiling on practice, defenders as range restriction. Untested directly.

The 1993 violin result is confirmed for the practice-alone totals (7,410 h vs 5,301 h vs 3,420 h by age 18; diary 24.3 h vs 9.3 h per week), but these are small groups, nominated by teachers, with retrospective recall.

A double-blind replication of the violin study did not replicate the best-vs-good difference (best 8,224 h vs good 9,844 h) but did replicate the large gap to less accomplished students (4,558 h); group effect eta2 .26 vs .48 originally.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Teacher-designed practice (the theoretical definition) did not explain more variance than simple solitary practice hours in the replication.

The hardest form of the 1993 claim, that nobody with less accumulated practice can catch up, is contradicted in the replication: most of the best violinists had less solo practice than the good-group mean.

Practice and genetics are not rival explanations: practice amount is itself 40-70% heritable in twin data, and practice lowers environmental, not genetic, variance in music discrimination (about 50% genetic remains).
Working memory capacity and general ability add predictive power beyond practice hours (practice 'necessary but not sufficient'); fluid intelligence matters less at higher chess skill (r .32 to .14).
Early specialisation is not the typical path to world-class level: world-class athletes and Nobel laureates show more early multidisciplinary activity. Abstract-level only.

Simulation-based medical education with deliberate practice shows large gains over traditional training (effect size 0.71) and AI tutoring with immediate feedback can raise a trained metric, but blinded global ratings may not move.
agent_test: None; transfer from tutor-optimised metric to blind rating is the test.

claim: LLM training loops that keep tasks at an intermediate pass rate (difficulty filtering, learnability rewards) speed up or improve RL: 2-6x faster, +several points on AIME, DAPO dynamic sampling in a 50 vs 30 AIME recipe. SPEED-RL counts screening cost and keeps total rollouts per prompt fixed, so the gain is not just more rollouts; no matched mid-pass vs random ablation exists.
agent_test: Not testable at inference; could mimic by choosing sub-problems whose solve rate is mid-range in a self-curriculum.
audit_note: Bae (up to +10 on AIME, +12% abstract), SPEED-RL (2-6x, screening counted in wall-clock, N_init+N_cont=N fixed) and DAPO (50 AIME) match; the closing 'no matched mid-pass vs random ablation exists' is an unverifiable absence claim (Bae compares balanced filtering with plain GRPO but not at matched compute).

claim: Self-generated curricula help even from zero data, with diminishing returns: R-Zero gains shrink per round and some subscores fall at round 3 as pseudo-label noise rises.
audit_note: R-Zero (Huang 2025) confirms +6.49 math avg over three iterations, collapse after iteration 3 and pseudo-label accuracy falling 79% to 63%; the exact per-subscore dips (MATH 79.8->78.0, GSM8K 92.12->89.08) could not be read reliably from the garbled table; Self-Challenging abstract supports the self-generated-data part.

claim: A graded self-built curriculum matters for an LLM agent: Voyager with a random curriculum found 93% fewer items and without self-verification 73% fewer. But Evo-Memory finds hard-to-easy task order beat easy-to-hard (ReMem avg 0.81 vs 0.77), so graded easy-first order is not supported as a general rule.
agent_test: Ablate ordering of sub-goals in the agent's plan at equal tokens.

claim: Feedback quality is the gate: with oracle labels LLM self-correction improves (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3; GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0), but intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonsenseQA 75.8 to 38.1).
agent_test: Run scaffold with and without an external verifier on the same items at equal tokens.
audit_note: Huang 2024 Tables 2-3 confirm all numbers (oracle: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9->84.3, GPT-4 HotpotQA 49.0->59.0; intrinsic CSQA 75.8->38.1); the researcher's evidence line c13 misread the table rows but the claim itself is right; Reflexion consistent.

claim: Step-level (process) feedback beats outcome feedback as a selection signal: best-of-1860 78.2% (PRM) vs 72.4% (ORM) vs 69.6% (majority vote).
agent_test: Compare step-level self-check vs final-answer check at equal tokens.

claim: Real-time expert-style feedback delivered by an LLM to humans can raise learning outcomes modestly (Tutor CoPilot +4 pp mastery, +9 pp for low-rated tutors).
Observational data link AI-assisted practice to self-regulated learning and performance (beta .47 and .39) but cannot show causation.

A named 'deliberate practice' LLM training recipe (DPPO) reports less forgetting than RL alone (MMStar 1.9 vs 24.8) but lacks a non-deliberate hard-example baseline; the label is analogy, not test of the theory.
Post-corrigendum, the 2014 meta-analysis gives deliberate practice r=.38 and 14% of variance overall (games 24%, music 23%, sports 20%, education 5%, professions 1%); the original 12% is superseded.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The corrected estimate of about 61% of variance (r about .78, from raw r=.54) depends on an assumed practice-recall reliability (0.6 in Ericsson and Harwell, 0.8 in Macnamara and Hambrick's re-correction); the direct data cited cover recent weeks or years (r .60-.75, de Bruin r(34)=.60; Ward 2007 found recall reliable only for about 5 years), and the lifetime-practice reliability of .7-.8 rests on an unreferenced statement rather than reported data.
audit_note: Ericsson and Harwell 2019 report r=.54 (29% of variance), which after correcting for attenuation (practice reliability .6, performance .8) is 61% of variance (r about .78, Macnamara and Hambrick 2020 Table 3), not 'corrected r=.61'; also 'none cover full careers' is too strong because an unreferenced Ericsson (2013) lifetime reliability of .7-.8 is cited.
claim_before_audit: The corrected r=.61 depends on an assumed practice-recall reliability (0.6-0.8); direct data exist only for recent weeks or years (r .60-.75, de Bruin r(34)=.60) and none cover full careers.

claim: No test has corrected the elite-only r (about .11, 1% of variance in elite athletes) for range restriction; both camps concede it lowers r, and chess fluid-intelligence splits (.32 vs .14) are confounded with age.

Inside one session, repeating the same task with feedback and rewriting the prompt/memory between attempts improves a frozen LLM agent (J-TTL average AUC 0.11 static vs 0.32 Reflexion vs 0.47 EvoTest); plain repetition with no update stays flat. No study matched tokens exactly.
agent_test: Equal-token test: scaffold with retry-and-rewrite vs best-of-N on a task with an external checker.
audit_note: EvoTest Table (avg AUC Static .11, Reflexion .32, EvoTest .47 for Gemini 2.5 Flash) and Reflexion external-signal setup match; 'no study matched tokens exactly' is an unverifiable absence statement.

claim: In-session self-improvement is bounded by the signal and the model: Reflexion fell on MBPP Python (0.80 to 0.77) with a 16.3% false-positive test rate; Dynamic Cheatsheet gives little or inconsistent gain with small models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5 Haiku); EvoTest's gain shrinks with a weaker evolver (Detective AUC 0.94 with o3, 0.68 with Qwen3-8B) but stays well above the static 0.21.
schema_part: G# (external check before trusting a retry)
agent_test: Run the loop with a noisy checker and a small model to find the break-even.
audit_note: Reflexion MBPP Python 0.80 to 0.77 with 16.3% false-positive rate and Dynamic Cheatsheet small-model weakness confirmed, but EvoTest says a small Qwen3-8B evolver stays 'substantially above' the static baseline (Detective AUC 0.68 vs 0.21), so 'little gain with small models' is wrong for EvoTest.
claim_before_audit: In-session self-improvement is bounded by the signal and the model: Reflexion fell on MBPP Python (0.80 to 0.77) with a 16.3% false-positive test rate; Dynamic Cheatsheet and EvoTest give little gain with small models.

claim: Memory plus more samples compound; samples alone do not: on WebArena MaTTS rose 49.7 to 55.1 (k=1 to 5) with memory vs 39.0-42.2 without, at equal k.
agent_test: Same-k comparison of memory vs no memory in a scaffold.

claim: Part of the apparent test-time-learning gain is instruction quality, not memory: Dynamic Cheatsheet AIME 2024 baseline 23.3, instructions-only 36.7, with memory 50.0 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet).
agent_test: Always include an instructions-only control when testing memory.
